- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with upward momentum.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often overpredicts; reduce forecast to avoid overreaction.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5–10% in 1–2 days); apply a 1–2 day lag correction to smooth out overreaction.
- In early forecast windows (e.g., 30d from recent data), model underestimates mean reversion; adjust by adding 0.5–1.5% to forecast for medium-term recovery.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with the dominant sentiment trend; align forecast to the most recent sentiment direction.
- For horizon > 14 days, model often underestimates upward momentum; apply a 1–3% upward bias if sentiment is positive and price is trending up.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending, model underestimates continuation; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to capture momentum.
